core.cache.note: SP-R02: bearer mode keeps a verified CacheRecordV3 in IndexedDB (signed artifacts only: the trust manifest and both documents, ETags, the unsigned hints that only tighten the gate), re-verified against the pins on every load (src/browser/bearer/session.ts); the sync-etag-304 transcript replays through it. On desktop the host's Node SDK holds the cache and the renderer reads it through the bridge.

core.bundle.note: Desktop through the Node Electron bridge (protocol v4 importBundle); browser verified in-page by client-core inspectBundle against a random device id kept in IndexedDB. The browser runner drives inspectBundle over every bundleCases vector in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

core.local.note: SP-15: localAdapter() (@polaris-key/react/local) serves the documents the build bundles and a fixed licence state with no fetch in reach: it takes no transport, and every verb that would dial rejects local-only. The gate, config, config.local, crash tags, the boot guard and boot() work offline; supports() answers runtime N/A for the rest. A test with a throwing fetch stub proves no call is made.

core.store.note: SP-R02: bearer mode's indexedDbStore (src/browser/bearer/store.ts) implements client-core's Store: the token in its own object store, the random device id and the cache in the offline record; status() reports backend indexeddb, degraded not-persistent unless navigator.storage.persisted(). The cookie session holds no credential, so a cookie page's supports() answers it runtime-unsupported. Device binding to a hardware anchor is a typed N/A in a browser: the device id is a random value in IndexedDB and there is no platform anchor to re-derive it from; on desktop the host's Node SDK binds it.

packs.apply.delta.note: @polaris-key/zstd-wasm's browser entry (wasm32, P = 30, memBudget at most 2^30); the window check runs in the applier. Never for a gated pack or a base over 100 MiB.

sync.keyring.note: U-38.2: the browser bearer engine's key ring (RingEngine, ui-core browser/ring) on client-core's sync crypto and WebCrypto. The seven keyring-* transcripts replay through it (test/transcripts.test.ts); test/keyring.test.ts pins create, unwrap of this device's wrap, wrap to another device, recover and set the recovery code, reset and adopt, the lock and the codec keys. The root is a non-extractable HKDF key in IndexedDB; its bytes live in memory for 300 s after a create or recovery. A browser unlocks only with the recovery code (Q8). A browser whose device keys are memory-only (WebKit) cannot create or reset a ring (the Worker needs registered keys): it unlocks with the code and keeps the root in memory, so every load asks for the code again. A cookie page, the local adapter and the desktop bridge answer the typed N/A (runtime, runtime, version): the host serves no ring verb yet.

connect.identity.note: CC-09.1: adapter.connect (ui-core browser/connect, bearer mode): identity({refresh}), current(), listDevices(), discoveryKeys() and leave(), over the page's DeviceKeyPort (IndexedDB, non-extractable) and client-core peer/cert. The roster, certificate and K_disc are one pkey.connect.v1 record in the page's IndexedDB (memory with memory-only keys, which need allowEphemeralKeys); K_disc is non-enumerable and in no error. The previous K_disc goes 24 h after first seen, on roster loss or re-key and on leave; a 3.5-day short-circuit, which refresh bypasses; one call at a time; an unreadable record is an error that leave clears. Sign-out and deactivation call leave() and fail closed; a cookie page answers the typed runtime N/A. The connect-identity* transcripts replay in test/transcripts.test.ts; test/connectIdentity.test.ts pins the rest.

connect.noise.note: client-core's peer/noise.ts over WebCrypto X25519 and AES-256-GCM, which the web relay sessions run (the DH of this device's key goes through DeviceKeyPort.dh); the browser runner drives every noise-vectors.json row in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (conformance/runners/browser/noiseVectors.browser.test.ts), and test/connectRelay.test.ts runs a full XXpsk0 admission between two devices.

connect.protocol.note: client-core's peer/ codecs (frame, record, relay, payload) and the PeerChannel session machine, which the web relay sessions run in mode a (test/connectRelay.test.ts: admission, 200 KB MORE reassembly, rekey-free close); the peer-matrix.json sections are driven by conformance/runners/node.

connect.lan.note: A browser or renderer has no sockets; the relay is its only path, and the host's Node SDK does the rest.

connect.relay.note: ui-core browser/connect (relay.ts, CC-09.2) behind adapter.cloudConnect and useCloudConnect(): connect.relayTicket() (the pkeyrt_ ticket, shape-checked, wss and the Worker's own host only; typed RelayError for relay_disabled, relay_paused with Retry-After capped at 3600 s, relay_quota_exceeded with its scope), a RelayService over the browser's WebSocket (pkey-relay.1, the ticket as the second subprotocol) with client-core's envelope codec, one PeerChannel per (peer, session) in the literal mode a (v and p never cross: assertRelayMode), backoff with jitter and a floor that resets only after 30 s stable, byte-capped session queues (peer_busy past 8 MiB; a WebSocket cannot be paused) and a bounded PeerDocs queue, a pushed RING through the identity replacement rules (keysStale, deferred refresh, one refresh a minute), a pushed TRUST verified against the usable pins with anti-rollback under the session's trust lock, and nothing secret reachable through JSON.stringify, enumerable fields or console. The relay code loads on the first start() (the React size budgets hold). The connect-relay-ticket and connect-relay-quota transcripts replay in test/transcripts.test.ts; test/connectRelay.test.ts pins the rest.

connect.links.note: A browser or renderer has no sockets; the relay is its only path, and the host's Node SDK does the rest.

connect.app.note: adapter.cloudConnect / useCloudConnect() (CC-09.2): start, stop, peers, refreshPeers, devices, open, onChannel, onNotice, status and onChange, with the relay as the only path (a page cannot discover devices on a LAN: connect.lan is the typed runtime N/A). A cookie page and the local adapter answer the typed runtime N/A, the desktop renderer the version N/A (its host runs the Node SDK). Sign-out and deactivation stop it before leaving the roster.
